column2: ENGLISH

Priviet, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

The Winds of Magic were given to the daughters of Kislev, and the law of the Khan-Queens is clear: no man is to touch them. Yet our sisters have felt the cold stir where it should not. [male_target.GetTitledName] of [male_target.Location.GetName] has been meddling with powers forbidden to him.

Find him. Bring the law of the Sisterhood to bear on him, before his tampering calls something worse down upon us all.

Signed, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
He will answer to the Sisterhood.
I have other matters to attend to.

You have followed the trail of frost and broken wards to its source: [the_accused.GetTitledName], a man pursuing what is forbidden to him by the law of Kislev. Whether he burns, is hollowed or walks free now rests with those who rule him. You will make sure they hear the Sisterhood's voice.
Let him be judged.
Justice has been done to [the_accused.GetTitledName]. The cold he stole has been taken back, and the Grand Ice Witches will hear of your diligence.
The law of the Khan-Queens holds.
[the_accused.GetTitledName] has been spared by a soft-hearted lord. The man walks free with his stolen magic, and the Sisterhood will know that you failed to stop it.
This is not over.

Priviet, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

We have learned of a girl with the gift in [recruit_to_be.Location.GetName]. [recruit_to_be.GetFirstName] remains outside our fold, and an untrained gift is a danger to her and everyone near her. Go to her and offer her a place among us.

Signed, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
I will speak with her.
Let another sister go.
You have arrived at [recruit_to_be.Location.GetName]. Frost forms on the windows wherever [recruit_to_be.GetFirstName] sleeps, and the servants whisper about it. It is time to send for her.
Bring her to me.

A woman in white furs has come to see you, and the air grows cold around her. She says she is of the Ice Witch Sisterhood, and that your gift has been felt from far away. If you come with her, she will teach you to master it, as the daughters of the Khan-Queens have done for a thousand years.
I will learn.
No. My life is my own.
[recruit_to_be.GetFirstName] has accepted your offer to become an Ice Witch. Her lessons begin at once.
How delightful.
[recruit_to_be.GetFirstName] has had the audacity to refuse you. The Sisterhood will not forget it.
Then let her gift freeze her.
The training of [recruit_to_be.GetFirstName] is well underway. The ice answers her now, if not always as she wishes. What should you teach her next?
Caution. The ice bites the careless.
Daring. An Ice Witch must not hesitate.
Focus. Discipline above all.

Your [GetFromRelation] spends long hours teaching you caution. Ice that is called carelessly does not stop where you want it to. She shows you the old scars on her own hands, white and smooth as frost.
I will be careful.
Your [GetFromRelation] drives you to experiment, to call the cold harder and faster than you dare. A witch who hesitates in battle dies, she tells you, while the snow whirls around you both.
I will not hesitate.
Your [GetFromRelation] teaches you to hold your mind still as a frozen lake. Even the simplest spell needs perfect discipline, she says, or it shatters.
Of course.
Your training is complete. The cold no longer hurts you. It obeys you. You have taken your place among the Ice Witches of Kislev, free to serve the land as you see fit.
Winter answers to me.
[From.GetFirstName]'s studies are done, and she has taken her place among her sisters. You taught her well.
Another daughter of the ice.

Priviet, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

Your sisters notice that you spend your days on idle things. The Lore of Ice is deep, and you have barely touched it. Give yourself to study, as an Ice Witch should.

Signed, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

Priviet, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

The Ice Witches have always stood beside the throne of Kislev. Give your days to ruling well, and show the boyars what a daughter of the Khan-Queens can do.

Signed, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

Priviet, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

The courts of Kislev are full of whispers, and the Sisterhood needs to hear them. Turn your attention to the secrets of those around you.

Signed, [From.GetTitledFirstName]

Priviet, [Root.GetSocietyRank]!

The Northmen and their dark gods press on our borders every year. Kislev needs witches who ride with its armies. Give yourself to war.

Signed, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
It will be done.
I will live as I choose.
You have given yourself to the study of the Lore of Ice, as your sisters asked.
You have given yourself to ruling, as your sisters asked.
You have turned your mind to the secrets of the court, as your sisters asked.
You have given yourself to war, as your sisters asked.
The Sisterhood will be pleased.
Hunt the Male Mage
A man is working magic forbidden to him by the law of Kislev. Find him and see him judged.
Recruit a Sister
A girl with the gift waits outside the Sisterhood. Bring her in and train her.
Study the Lore
Your sisters want you to take up the Scholarship focus.
Serve the Throne
Your sisters want you to take up the Rulership focus.
Hear the Whispers
Your sisters want you to take up the Intrigue focus.
Ride to War
Your sisters want you to take up the War focus.
You have grown restless these past few weeks, and once again you cannot sleep. You pace in circles about your room while the wind howls around the castle.
Perhaps I should explore the castle a little?

You wander the twisting halls of the castle, peering into the occasional room and finding little of note. But in one forgotten chamber a great wardrobe stands hidden in the shadows, and you cannot shake the feeling that something cold and patient is watching you from inside it.
It's getting late... I should get back to my room.
Where did this come from?
Without taking your eyes off the wardrobe, you back out of the room. Only when it is out of sight do you turn and run to your quarters, slam the door and leap into your bed.
Close your eyes and get some sleep.

You creep closer. The wardrobe breathes cold. Snowy forests and frozen rivers are carved into its wood and iron, so finely that you cannot look away. You reach out to touch it, and before you know what you are doing you have opened the door and crawled inside. The door shuts firmly behind you.
How deep is this thing?!

You stumble out of the back of the wardrobe into snow. The first thing you notice is not the black pines or the drifts, but the cold: a biting, unbearable cold, worse than the deepest winter in the oblast. Teeth chattering, you wrap yourself in some old furs from the wardrobe and follow a path through the trees until it forks. Which way now?
Take the left fork.
Take the right fork.
You follow the path for what seems like hours. Your fingers and toes go numb, and you begin to think longingly of the warm bed waiting in your room.
I've been here far too long, time to get home!

The path opens onto a clearing packed with ruined houses huddled around a frozen well. No smoke rises from any chimney. As you walk towards the middle of the dead village, dread fills your bones: something is waiting just around the next corner. You catch a glimpse of it, a hunched thing of fur and too many teeth, sniffing at the snow.
Make a run for it!
Hide! Quick!
Without a moment's hesitation you turn and run for the wardrobe. When you are just a few feet away you glance back, but whatever it was has not followed you.
Quickly climb back inside.
making it back safely.

The beast sees you at once. A serrated claw sinks into your thigh as you try to flee, dragging you towards its jagged maw. You kick free, struggle to your feet and stumble to the wardrobe, too terrified to look back. You fall out onto the castle floor covered in blood, and as you cry out for help the wardrobe slowly sinks into the wall behind you.
Help! I'm hurt!
it seeing you!

You duck into the nearest doorway and crawl under the rotten frame of a bed. You wait without a sound for what feels like hours, until the presence fades away, and then you creep out of your hiding place.
Take a look around.
going unnoticed.

The room is dark and furred with frost, and you know something terrible happened here. As you turn to leave you notice a pale blue glow from a great gemstone set into the mantel above the dead hearth. It is cold as the heart of winter, and it seems to be waiting for you.
What's this?
Reach out and touch the gemstone.
Leave it where it is and get out of here.
As you lay your hand on the stone it flashes with a blinding blue light, and a cold power floods through you, sharp and wonderful. You cry out before you can stop yourself!
Head back to the wardrobe, that thing might have heard you...

As you climb out of the wardrobe a wave of sickness hits you and you collapse, the room spinning around you. It takes a long time to come back to your senses. The wardrobe is gone, and the morning sun is shining through the window...
Was it all a dream?
Shard of the Winter Gem
A splinter of blue ice that never melts, broken from a gem in a land that may not exist. It is always cold to the touch, and on winter nights it hums faintly.
Rebellious Erengrad

The great trading port of Erengrad broke away from its rulers in Kislev during the succession crisis several decades ago. Its burghers have never claimed to stand above the [Root.GetTitle], but they have set a dangerous example for every other would-be secessionist, and their refusal to submit only feeds the anger at court.\n\nA punitive expedition would be justified, though the boyars and the Northmen alike may call it tyranny. On the other hand, the burghers' coin could buy a great deal.
The rebellious burghers have defied my will for too long!
Their coin could make a very convincing argument.
Fate of the Erengrad Veche

The heart of the burghers' rule in Erengrad has always been the Veche, the great hall where their council meets. Destroying it would break their will and silence all talk of self-rule. Sparing it would be seen as a gesture of the [Root.GetTitle]'s mercy, and would do much to bind the city's loyalty to Kislev.
The Veche burns. Their defiance cannot go unpunished.
The Veche shall remain at the pleasure of the [Root.GetTitle].
The Kislevite Ultimatum

The ruler in Kislev has given us a choice: pay a heavy tribute, or face the might of the Tzar's armies. There is reason to think the threat is empty posturing, but refusing still risks the independence of our republic.
Our independence is worth a few coins.
This is an outrage!
Threats Pay Off

The burghers of Erengrad have agreed to pay a hefty sum, and to go on paying, to keep their city independent. They are not happy to part with their coin, but the threat of invasion no longer hangs over them.
Gold flows north, as it should.
Erengrad Unmoved
The arrogant burghers of Erengrad have refused your just demand. To your most generous offer the patricians have answered only with insults to your dignity as their rightful sovereign.
Their folly will soon be made clear to them.
The Kremlin Guard

The Kremlin Guard proved themselves formidable warriors in the days of Igor the Terrible. You have gathered many of their number back into a personal guard loyal only to the [Root.GetTitle].\n\nThey will be a powerful shock force against Kislev's many enemies, and their foreign roots should keep them out of the palace intrigues that are so common in [Root.Capital.GetName].
They shall serve me well.
